God; your counsels have drawn near, says King Jacob; having well explained the calling of the nations in due time, promising to make the desert into a forest and the dry land into waterways, with cedars and boxwood and other plants, and to make his hand marvelous, saying, as the creator of such great things, he again addresses the makers of idols and such craftsmen, and says their judgment is near; judgment, that is, the punishment owed to them; namely, shame and remorse; for by God's holy vote and just judgment, they would be punished as having deceived those under heaven and introduced untrue counsels; for they taught those on earth to speak to wood, saying, 'You are my father,' and to stone, 'You begot me'; with these things, God says their counsels have drawn near, that is, have come to an end, as he dispels the deception and the mist of ignorance, and not one of their false names remains, but the Lord and God in truth, and the King of Jacob, that is, of those from the blood of Israel; through these things, he brings to remembrance the signs that have occurred, concerning the redemption of those from Israel, through which the power of his inherent divine authority is well known, or his unsurpassed superiority; let them draw near and promise what will happen to you, or what things were before; say, and we will set our mind and know what the last things and the things to come are

Tell us what is coming in the end, and we will know that you are gods. Do good or evil, and we will marvel and see where you are from and what your work is. They were chosen from the earth as an abomination. It is characteristic of divine and ineffable glory to know everything and be ignorant of nothing, neither past nor present nor future. And indeed, through the all-wise Moses, before the creation of this world, and the things evident to those on earth, he says: 'In the beginning, God created the heaven and the earth.' The earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss, and he describes the creation of the world in detail. But our Lord Jesus Christ, who spoke through Moses, also announced to us the things in the end times, as his disciple says: 'We await new heavens and a new earth, and his promises.' It is also written: 'Nothing will be hidden from me?' For the word of God is truly living and evident.
pass_b_english: God says that the counsels of idolaters have drawn near, as King Jacob affirms, and He has well explained the calling of the nations in due time, promising to transform the desert into a forest and the dry land into waterways, complete with cedars, boxwood, and other plants, and to make His hand marvelous, saying, as the creator of such great things, He makes His hand marvelous by doing so.

By doing so, He addresses the makers of idols and such craftsmen, warning them that their judgment is near, which refers to the punishment owed to them, namely, shame and remorse, for by God's holy vote and just judgment, they would be punished as having deceived those under heaven and introduced untrue counsels.
They have taught people to speak to wood, saying, 'You are my father,' and to stone, 'You begot me' (Isaiah 44:24).

With these things, God says their counsels have drawn near, that is, have come to an end, as He dispels the deception and the mist of ignorance, and not one of their false names remains, but the Lord and God in truth, and the King of Jacob, that is, of those from the blood of Israel.

Through these things, He brings to remembrance the signs that have occurred, concerning the redemption of those from Israel, and through these signs, the power of His inherent divine authority is well known, or His unsurpassed superiority.
Let them draw near and promise what will happen to you, or what things were before; say, and we will set our mind and know what the last things and the things to come are (Isaiah 41:22-23).
Do good or evil, and we will marvel and see where you are from and what your work is, for you were chosen from the earth as an abomination.

It is characteristic of divine and ineffable glory to know everything and be ignorant of nothing, neither past nor present nor future, as it is written: 'Nothing will be hidden from me?' (Jeremiah 23:24).

This is evident in the words of the all-wise Moses, who described the creation of the world in detail, saying: 'In the beginning, God created the heaven and the earth' (Genesis 1:1), and our Lord Jesus Christ, who spoke through Moses, also announced to us the things in the end times, as His disciple says: 'We await new heavens and a new earth, and His promises' (2 Peter 3:13).
For the word of God is truly living and evident.
